doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Hearing himself on the radio and commercial work
summary: He prefers musical dates to commercial ones he did to pay the mortgage.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Now did you ever, you must have heard yourself on the radio quite a bit with all the stuff you were doing, not just under your own name.
Oh yeah with other guys. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
Here comes Herb Alpert on the radio, and I’m on that. There must have been a certain amount of satisfaction in that.
Yeah, especially if it was something musical, right. If it was something too commercial, I wouldn’t even want to listen. I just went in to do the job so I could make the mortgage payment.
It wasn’t something that you’d call your neighbor over and say listen—
Exactly. Yeah right. But there were some lovely things that I did that I’m proud of. Can we stop for a second, I want to get my—
